definition: The gradual degradation of a deployed model's performance over time as real-world data distributions shift away from the training data.
details: Model drift necessitates ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and periodic retraining or fine-tuning of production models to maintain performance as the environment and user behavior evolve.

explainer.lead: The gradual degradation of a deployed model's performance over time as real-world data distributions shift away from the training data. It matters because maintaining performance requires ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and periodic retraining or fine-tuning.

tiers.eli5: The world slowly changes, so yesterday's well-tuned model gradually stops fitting today's situation.
tiers.practitioner: Teams monitor and evaluate production models and retrain or fine-tune periodically as environments and user behaviour evolve. A pitfall is treating a deployed model as finished rather than something that degrades.
tiers.paperLevel: Performance degrades as real-world data distributions shift from training data; mitigation is monitoring, evaluation, and periodic retraining or fine-tuning.

explainer.example: A deployed model's accuracy slips over months as user behaviour changes, prompting retraining.
